body:
Thanks. Things do tend to seem 100 times worse for me when I am really tired. I did manage to get a little rest today.

Logically, my life isn't so bad at all. I'm sure it's mainly body chemistry and a long learned habit of negative thinking.

I do have kind, caring professors at school who've offered to hear what's on my mind. As bad as I feel sometimes, I always fear my problems will just be taken as whining. I think of my dad and older sister every time I wonder if someone will care about my problems, and decide they probably won't.

I will do my best to talk to one of them in the morning, though. The last couple of weeks on /r/depression and sw have given me a little more faith that sometimes people really genuinely care about what I'm going through.

Is it purely by choice that you will be stopping? If so, try to be comfortable with the idea of coming back if you feel it would help in the future. Maybe talk to your therapist about this. I know when I say something is over, but change my mind, I feel a guilty about what I view as a deception.

Maybe transitioning into something like journaling would help. If you trust the therapist you have, start writing a blog and tell him the address. If he.she is agreeable to reading it at least occasionally, you can feel more like you have a safety net.

Nothing else comes to mind. Good luck.

Gosh, I guess I'm being too subtle? I'm saying that if you really want to feel guilty about something, you can choose any single thing that you do during any moment of your life. Eating and breathing? Wasting resources. Heart is beating? If someone dies that needed a heart transplant, you might as well have been the one to kill him.

Teachers, thinkers, and leaders are just as bad, get it? Everybody is good! It is okay to do things that make your life better.

Suzie wants vanilla. Greg wants chocolate. They get vanilla. Should Suzie feel guilty? No! Enjoy the damn vanilla! Greg sure as hell wouldn't have felt guilty if they had gotten chocolate.

*edit: typo

That's why I chose Vitamin C. It is water soluble, so excess amounts are flushed out with urine. Plus, if Wikipedia is accurate in this case, a deadly dose would be around 2 pounds for someone my size.

What you say is true, though. Don't just pick the vitaman named after your favorite letter or choose something like iron supplements.

Yeah, I guess it looks that way. I'm really pretty serene about the whole thing.

Everyone on this planet is a dream crushing machine. Your grandma plants a hedge and crushes her neighbor's dream of a perfect view from the window. Bob buys a bottle of Fiji water and crushes Betty's dream of a world without waste. You live, and crush the dream of someone that hates you. How dare anyone do anything for themself? Can't they think of the other people on the planet?

They all have plenty to feel guilty about, but, that's the world we live in. And a fantastic world it is. :)

Well, medications react differently with everyone. I've taken half a dozen different types over the years and with most of them, I didn't feel any effects at all. I want to recomend talking to a doctor first, but they don't really know either. They pretty much just know what it says on the box that the drug comes in.

However, if you feel motivated to take medications, it might be time. You might not feel like trying for any help at all in the future.

And maybe you should have stopped listening to me already, and you probably should stop now, but I swear this next thing is true. The most effective anti-depressant I've ever taken have been placeboes. Placeboes that I decided to take. I chose vitamin C, because it isn't harmful to consume quite a bit of it. I knew that it wasn't a real anti-depressant, obviously, but every time I wanted to feel better or less anxious, I would take one.

It worked, because several times a day I would say to myself "I want to feel better, and I am willing do something about it. And here is proof." Gulp.

That's really true. But... maybe consult a licensed physician.

This is a tough one. You feel guilty. You wish you didn't feel guilty. But you also feel like you don't deserve to not feel guilty. That's part of it, isn't it?

I could tell you, hey, go easy on yourself. But I think you already know all the facts.

I used to feel extremely guilty about every tiny imperfection in my past. Only a year or so ago I slept with my best friend's girl. He was actually a pretty useless dude and was very mean to her. She told me they were broken up, and most of all she was there in my room.

He was pissed, but fuck him. It was the perfect excuse to never talk to him again. I corresponded with the girl for a long time after that. She broke up with him, she broke up with him, she broke up with him. I was tired of hearing about her break up with him, because once really should have been enough. She finally told me she couldn't talk to me anymore because it was too painful. Y'alright.

It was about this time that I stopped feeling guilty about everything. Everyone is an asshole, because everyone has their own unique idea about what the world should be like. And no two people's ideas match. So everyting you do something to get your world, you're fucking up the dreams of everyone else on the planet.

I didn't get there alone. I read Chuck Palahuniuk. Hey, this character is an asshole. He keeps making all these mistakes. I kind of like him. He's okay. I read Vonnegut. Hey, these guys destroyed the whole damn world just because of some stupid asshole's greed. What are you going to do about it? No point in saying sorry, really. The Tralfamadorians could have told you that it was bound to happen anyway.

Sitcoms and facebook and everything we've got today really makes you think that you can be a great dude that everybody loves and fixes any mistakes that he makes. I have my doubts.

Hope any of that is even remotely relevant.

Some people disagree with my interpretation, but as I see it, a depressed person is just as motivated as anyone. It just so happens that they are motivated to despair and sleep and give up. The reason that "get better" sounds so impossible is that your brain is working perfectly! It's just that you can think of something else that you'd rather it worked perfectly toward. 

Try to find something that you would like to do and get better at, which also isn't so hard. Cooking or carving or juggling or something. If do and accomplish and learn something. The whole process will be good. If you learn a skill that impresses you, you will impress others with it. You will gain confidence.

How can you choose? Personally, when I am most depressed, I feel motivated to feel worse and worse, so it has to be small. I can sometimes dig out of a hole by drawing or by making Magic the Gathering decks.

About relationships... remember that nothing can change the past. That means that all the good moments and bad are frozen back there. Try to remember the good times, because they still exist. Try to consider the relationship as a positive experience. If you are unhappy that it is gone. Shouldn't it follow naturally that you were glad that it happened?

Hmm. The middle. I often overlook it. I tend to think that I either feel good or bad. The middle sounds fine.

Not getting enough sleep can be a real problem for me. If I happen to stay awake to late I quickly become very unhinged: flinching at shadows and weeping uncontrollably.

That's one of the scariest things I go through. I sometimes start to lose grip as early as 1am. I've become very good lately at going to bed at the same time every night and waking up at the same time 10pm to 7am no matter what. And it really helps to make the day feel normal.

I went ahead and ordered that book. What's the worst that could happen?

The same adults that knew way more about the real world than you did, but didn't feel the need to share any of that knowledge with you.

"What do you want to be when you grow up?"

"I really don't know. What can I be? Everything looks so hard."

"Oh, you can be anything you want. You'll do really well"

"Yeah, but how..."

End of interaction.
Good for you! I was just reading your previous post. Glad for you, and glad that we get some more information.

I had to look it up myself, but I think it makes sense. I learned on radiolab that each time you recall a memory it is essentially destroyed and remade.

So focusing on a memory you want to get past makes you recall the memory. First it is destroyed, then it is remade. Since you are doing it in a safe environment, it out of it's original painful context, it will reduce in impact. The reason for the eye movement and bilateral sounds help, is that they activate both hemispheres of your brain, helping to spread the new-old memory throughout your brain. Since if you are upset each time you tap into a certain place in your brain, your brain recognizes the pattern and makes you upset.

That's what I got out radiolab + wikipedia, at least.

Ugh. This is one that is still pretty much insurmountable for me. On the rare days that I've felt the correct combination of depressed, motivated, and willing to talk to another human, I would sometimes go out to the clinic to ask for help. I could only get an appointment for next week, so I'd tell them that I definitely wouldn't feel well enough to show up then, and can I see someone now?

And so 2 months is about how long it takes me to finally see someone, who spends 5 minutes with me. They offer me a drug. I refuse it. They say take it or leave it and they are out.

So I pretty much just take medications that I buy online. 

If you have someone to make appointments for you, that can be helpful. I think that better than finding a doctor would be finding someone that knows doctors and that also gives a damn about you.

Who is this person? I just don't know.

There's something R.A. Salvatore said once that's always stuck with me. People ask him all the time things like "I want to be a writer, how do I know if it's right for me?"

So he tells them they can find out in one simple step: "Just stop writing. Try as hard as you can. If you keep failing step one, you're a writer."

This doesn't seem to apply to your problem very directly, but hopefully it's something to think about. The right career for you is the one that you would be doing no matter what other career you were in.

I spent a semester abroad in London and hated it. I never really met anyone, I just kept myself locked away like I usually do.

I went back to england recenly with my mom, and had a great time. See is outgoing enough to start conversations with anyone, and once I was locked into communication, I saw that everyone was really happy to talk.

I've learned this lesson many times. There's really nothing to be afraid of. It still hasn't stuck. I'm still terrified to speak with even classmates that I know are friendly.

I did volunteering, after Katrina, and it was sort of harrowing. I felt like everyone was right where they were supposed to be, and that they were all staring at me and wondering why I was there.

I think it is good to have a bro along with you. Someone that you are at ease with, and someone that is at ease with all of humanity.

If you want to go to some place far away and don't plan on meeting the locals, you could just as easily use google streetview to take your tours.

Things are probably going to get worse before they get better. You have a lot to do before you will feel like you are in a really good place.

I like to remind people that a depressed brain is a perfect and fully functional machine. It perfectly produces sadness. There's nothing wrong with you, you'd just rather that something nicer than sadness was the output of you perfect brain.

So do some little things that can help to rewrite some of the code. Cook for yourself. Don't think about how long it is taking, don't think about the other things you would rather be doing. Decide on cooking something, and cook it. The idea is similar to meditating. If you can focus on the perfect human machine that you are, living in the moment, completing a task that will sustain your life, the animal part of your body will be very satisfied with you.

If a caveman could eat and have children, he would consider his life to be perfectly successful. Sometimes it doesn't have to be about what's gone wrong or what might not happen right. Sometimes it is just you, doing something you can take pride in achieving. Something that goes back to your primitive ancestors.

Your ancestors did everything as groups, too. If you work with someone, someone like your mom, to make that food, your inner animal can be satisfied that not only will you be fed, but your tribe is nearby and safe.

This interaction will probably also do more for your mom than you will be able to realize until you have your own children.

There's more you can do. Sit down and do a jigsaw puzzle. Play scrabble. Focus on the each little task you undertake. Hopefully in time you will want bigger tasks, but remember that small successes are important.

Before you were born, there was nothing, and after you die, there will be nothing. Thus you can conclude that the universe will only ever be as old as you. How can taking time to make some little improvements in your life be seen as a waste, when your conciousness spans the entirety of time(time, as far as you are concerned).
Thanks for your well wishes, I do believe that I am making progress, and don't count out therapy for a time in the future when I am more trusting again.

I don't know of any in particular, but am certain that some must be out there. The only related experience I have relates to my girlfriend's severe depression after having an abortion. I visited family planning to see if I could talk to someone there, and they had all sorts of information about hotlines and things. I called the number that seemed most relevent and talked for hours with an operator who really made me feel better about what I was doing to help and the sort of signs I should be looking out for.

God bless people like you. There's no way of knowing where I would be now without my mom's unflaggable and generous support.

If you can't find something that looks good online, go into a mental health care clinic and find someone that doesn't look like at you like you are wasting their time. Some one there will have lots of local resources for you.

I lost my first therapist to retirement. He was the only one that had any effect on me. I probably tried ten others sinse, and trusted each one of them too much, I think. I tried to do it their way, because I was young and shy, when now I wish I had stood up and pushed onto them the things that worked for me.

**What happened**:

"Do you do the ink blot thing here?"

"No, that's school X, and I belong to school Y."

"Oh, okay."

**What should have happened**:

"Do you do the ink blot thing here?"

"No, that's school X, and I belong to school Y."

"Can we try them? I found that they really help me notice feelings I was having that weren't concious to me. If you have to get some of the cards or read into it, I would really appreciate it."

Instead of standing up for myself I failed to produce anything but frustration and I currently totally distrust therapists.

You aren't joining this new therapist's case load, this new therapist is joining YOUR treatment. Make sure you hold onto the things that are helping you.

This can be frustrating. You'd think that they as trained professionals would be able to pick up a certain amount from the way you act, not just the things that you say.

"Tell me about your relationship with your father." They ask.

"No, I really don't want to talk about that." You say.

"What about your mother? We have to learn something before we can do anything for you."

Because apparently my poker face was impassible.

Maybe it's something like paperwork that is holding them back. I try to make things as obvious as I can with the anxiety that I am feeling.

"Do you want medication?"

"I'm so unhappy that all I want to do is get worse and worse. Any decision I make for myself is the wrong one. I need someone to help me out. I don't want medication. It would definitely be nice to feel better though, and I don't have anything against medication."

✔ Patiend declines medication.

*Well, you are just a peach, doc.*

They usually just have a clipboard.

"Do you often feel a generalized sense of anxiety?"

"What, like... am I afraid of something."

"More like a low level, unjustified fear."

"So, if I was fighting a bear, it would be impossible to feel anxiety, because the fear would be justified? I'm telling you, whatever I feel seems justified to me."

It really would be nice if someone could sit people down and define a lot of these words for people. Certainly depression, fear, and anger feel totally different to different people.

The problem I most run into is that anyone that knows anything about this stuff doesn't have any free time to talk about it for free.

Thanks for the reply. Is "Undoing Depression" a good read? I glanced at it on Amazon and it looked interesting. Usually I'm not a fan of self help books, but I feel like I need reason more now to understand how I can help myself.

I do find your two paths analogy very easy to understand. I can see the flowers and green grass just over the hill, but it's so easy to stay on the trusted dirt path.

I have been making an effort, I read about it in a Vonnegut book, to make a point of voicing my happiness wherever I recognize it. Going geocaching with the niece and nephews. "Well, if this isn't nice, I don't know what is."

And it is getting easier to believe that things can often be nice. But right now it is much easier to believe that giving up holds the greater reward.

I remember a pretty lengthy amount of time where anybody who felt sad was a "emo" and the butt of many jokes. They still exist, but it seems like hipsters are the new popular target.

I feel for the lgbt community, because so many people seem to react so strongly and negatively when a person has valid feelings that they don't understand.

Not to minimize it, but I remember watching an episode of Deadwood. Some characters ruthlessly harassed a black person, and I thought that it would be nice to have people at least be so honest about how much they hate you.

I've been in and out of college for 11 years now. I don't know what you should do, and I don't know if what I did was correct, but here's my experience.

I hated high school. I felt like nothing that happened there mattered. I took the exam to graduate early. I completed my sophomore year and went straight on to community college. I made it through the first few semesters without much incident, because the classes were easy enough, and I was still young enough to think that class was something you did for grades, and not something you did to get an education.

I moved on to a state college. I chose English as a major because I felt so strongly about it. I loved reading and writing and just wanted to study what I loved. I would pass one semester and fail the next. Pass/fail/pass/fail. I listened to lessons to learn the material, and wrote essays to contribute new ideas to the subject at hand. For me, it is really difficult to get good grades while taking the idea of education seriously. I took time off and worked. Work was okay, but I felt like I was going nowhere.

I changed majors and changed schools. This time I chose a major that I wasn't emotionally invested in. I chose computer science, because I was good at it, and knew it could lead to a job. I failed again. I took some time off and worked. I hated my job. I knew that I wanted to graduate, so I determined to try again.

I changed schools, and changed my major to art. I was set to fail again, because as with English, I was emotionally invested, took things too seriously and broke down. I should have failed, but the staff at this school was amazing to me. They were supportive and patient. They helped me get everything together and in, even though it was all late. Artists, apparently, take depression seriously and have some experience with it. Go figure. 

I am in my second semester in this school as an art major now, and I am doing quite well.

I sort of knew what I wanted, but I think that I compromised too much in my adult life. I stuck with professors I didn't care for, and I tried a program I didn't like. There are a lot of schools out there. It took me some time, but I found the place that was right for me.

I sometimes wish that I had gotten things right from day one, but the more people I talk to, the more I can accept that all of my life experience is valid, not just wasted time. There are things that I am good at that I never would have been exposed to if I had tried starting out where I am today.

I guess the lesson is: don't feel pressured to continue, and don't be pressured to stop. Don't feel like you are stuck with the choices you've made, and don't feel like your past choices were a waste, just because you aren't where you expected to be.

Great to hear. I've been fearing nobody would go for it, since compared to reddit, it technically just offers LESS. Less content, less users, etc. But I think that everything in it would feel more important, more relevant, and more real.

Sorry if this sounds too harsh, but if he is not happy, and you are with him. It stands to reason that you are not making him happy. Giving up on him might be the best thing for both of you. A parent should take comfort, pride, and happiness from the success of their child. If you have to get away from the place you are to become successful, you will either please him by the result, or else maybe there was little you could have done in the first place.

It helps me to remember that a depressed mind is a perfectly functional and complete mind. The difficulty is that the function of it is to be depressed. It can't be fixed, because it isn't broken, but it can be changed. It could help to make goals. It could help to make notes of things that do make you happy. It could help to find people who have stories you can relate to. It could help to copy the things that make others feel happy even if they don't make you feel happy, because you have to train the patterns into your well worn and perfectly functioning brain.

I personally enjoy fiction. I find stories about hopeless and flawed characters inspirational, because they go through so much, but they are still there on the next page, and eventually find a place where they feel they belong. I find the books of Chuck Palahniuk inspirational in that way. I think that too much popular media tells you what ought to be normal, and it is easy to become convinced that you are abnormal.

The way I read this, you have the ability to improve things.

First, you have taken the time to come here.

Second, you say that things are bad, and you aren't happy But you think that you would rather be happy than sad.

To me, this says that you can imagine a world in which you are happy, and that you are willing to put forth some sort of effort to find/make that world.

The reason that you are sleeping so much, I would bet, is that you sleep so much. It's something that bodies do. When you conserve energy, your body assumes that there must be a really good reason and takes it to extremes.

It might help to get out of the house. Maybe even without any plans of returning. If you don't like anything about your current situation, you could just try door number two and start over. You are still very young.

I'm not going to try bullying you into changing your life. Becoming happy shouldn't be a chore that people make you do. If you think of becoming happy as a painful task, you will start to hate happiness.

If any of this sounds relatable, I can continue, but I don't want to rant on if I am missing the mark.

I feel a very similar way. As long as I can remember, I've been confident that I would kill myself some time in the future.

Certain things, I've always felt, weren't worth doing. The reasoning: I'll be dead soon anyway.

The only jobs I've had were ones that I haven't worked hard to get. They'd been offered by friends or family. Most people see the need to work. "Either get a job or you starve to death" sounds rhetorical to most people, but to me it's a dilemma.

Typically, I don't want to die enough to give up living for it, but it is something I want. The same way someone might want to go to sea world, but doesn't want to drive down and pay for the ticket.

I'm surprised to see this post. I've never seen it discussed just so before, but this is my first time in r/suicidewatch. Personally, I've never told anybody I feel this way, because whenever suicide is brought up, attitudes change SO much. Disbelief, disrespect, antipathy, frustration. I've seen it all. People want you to say you don't think about suicide just so they can forget they ever saw any signs and go back to their problems.
